findings.summary: Plan 26's evidence/artifact/persistence layer (runtime/langgraph_factory/evidence.py, artifacts.py, persistence.py) was already deterministic and passing (63/63, then 64/64 after this attempt's own new test) before this node's changes; both owned test files were run twice from a clean state and produced identical pass counts each time (item 2/8). A new evidence_determinism.v1.yaml contract (2 claims) exercises the real, unmocked EvidenceStore.append -> write_audit_report path three times inside this node's own evidence scope and requires byte-identical stdout every time -- the payload carries only fixed run_id/episode_id/activation_id/node_id/phase fields, never a timestamp, tempfile path, or random id, so this is a genuine determinism proof, not a tautology. A new requirements_lineage.v1.yaml contract (8 claims) encodes the full seven-layer denominator this node's prompt item 6 requires (current user approval, approved v2 specification, Plans 20-22, retained PM postmortem product requirements, code, tests, product evidence), each layer checked against real, existing repository artifacts (spec_approval.v4.yaml, spec v4, Plans 20/21/22, the six-plus-module code/test set, and this node's own evidence), plus a self-consistency requirement_ids_cover claim so a layer id can never be referenced without a declared, falsifiable requirement backing it -- this is the mechanically-checkable form of 'the final audit must fail if any layer is omitted' N90 will consume.

Added tests/runtime/test_plan26_evidence.py::test_audit_report_never_claims_a_log_event_that_was_never_appended (item 3): a permanent negative regression guard for the historical PM-11/PM-12 false-claim pattern ('unit/workbook topology implemented but not registered in build_curriculum_factory_graph()'), generalized to N50's own owned layer -- seeds only the 'activations' evidence log, proves the write_audit_report() output for the never-appended 'executions' log honestly shows record_count 0 / status PASS / file_digest null, and that its per-log object carries no field capable of asserting a claim beyond what record_count/status/high_water_mark/file_digest mechanically say about real bytes on disk.

scan_node.py --node N50_EVIDENCE_AUDIT_CONTROLS genuinely failed on first real run, in the same shape N40 independently hit: tests/runtime/test_plan26_persistence.py's own forbidden-import guard (test_persistence_module_imports_no_product_or_model_module) legitimately named 'google.generativeai' as a forbidden import target, which the blunt, non-semantic retired_provider_test_scan term scan cannot distinguish from a live reference. Per this node's own prompt ('Remove every retired-provider reference from its owned active persistence test and keep the zero-occurrence test scan green'), fixed by asserting absence via the shared module-name suffix ('generativeai', '_genai') instead of the retired provider's own name -- strictly broader, not weaker. scan_node.py --node N50_EVIDENCE_AUDIT_CONTROLS now reports zero violations across all five of this node's scanned files.
